networkHosts.artifact: Node headers and libs for a from-source native compile
networkHosts.observed: node-gyp's default dist URL, reached whenever the header cache is cold. NOT observed in the 311-package corpus run: that harness sets `npm_config_nodedir` to the provisioned Node root, as nub does, so node-gyp never fetched. Absence there is not evidence the entry is unnecessary — it is evidence the corpus did not exercise a cold header cache. `fetchedBy` is matched against aube's INSTALLER-RESOLVED name, so this entry admits the `node-gyp` package's own lifecycle spawn and nothing else: a native-build dependency that shells `node-gyp rebuild` is spawned under ITS OWN name and needs its own entry. The demand is real for that whole class and this table cannot express it as a class — recorded here rather than widened, because `npm_config_nodedir` means the cold-cache fetch does not arise under nub.

packageGrants.mechanism: scripts/postinstall.js does three things, and each masks the next: it calls process.chdir(INIT_CWD); createDefaultGeneratedThrowFiles unconditionally mkdirs path.join(__dirname, '../../../.prisma'), a sibling of @prisma in the package's own enclosing node_modules; then it re-execs the prisma CLI as `prisma generate`, which reads the consumer's prisma/ schema directory. The generated client lands inside package_dir and needs no grant.
packageGrants.observed: EPERM mkdir <own node_modules>/.prisma, then EPERM uv_cwd on chdir(INIT_CWD), then EPERM reading the consumer's prisma/ schema. Verified by artifact, not exit code: a generated client of 71282 B carrying a per-run schema nonce, against absent output and 2 EPERMs without the grants. Presence alone is not a valid check here — the script writes throw-stubs before every guard, so it exits 0 having generated nothing.

packageGrants.mechanism: Its postinstall runs `indefinitely-typed`, which computes path.resolve(cwd, '../..'), asserts that directory is named node_modules, then mkdirs @types there and copySyncs each --folder argument into it. The write target is <own node_modules>/@types — the same enclosing-node_modules sibling shape as Prisma, under a different name.
packageGrants.observed: EPERM mkdir <own node_modules>/@types. With the grant, 20 copied type folders present; without it, absent.

packageGrants.mechanism: config/scripts/postinstall.js reads the CONSUMER's package.json for msw.workerDirectory, returns silently if absent, and otherwise re-execs its own CLI with cwd set to INIT_CWD to copy mockServiceWorker.js into each listed directory. The directories come from the field rather than a literal because msw imposes no convention — the consumer picks them.
packageGrants.observed: EPERM uv_cwd. The cwd need bites first: without projectCwd the child dies in uv_cwd before it reads the field at all. With the grants, msw's worker script is present; without them, absent.

notGranted.comment: Documentation only. Nothing in this object is compiled into any allowlist; it records hosts that a real install was measured to need and that were not admitted, so a contributor can see the bar before opening a PR. A build-time check keeps this list and networkHosts disjoint. Entries carry the same provenance fields as networkHosts, because an evidenced candidate is what makes a later promotion reviewable — `observedUrl` in particular is what a path-scoped grant would have to be written against.

hosts.requester: cube-js native installer (`Cube.js Native Installer`); 46 corpus packages total, 14 of them blocking
hosts.detail: The demand is real and measured, and the refusal is NOT about the download. github.com carries `git-receive-pack` — an authenticated write on the same hostname — and CI routinely hands lifecycle scripts a token with push rights, so a host-level grant opens a push path rather than only a fetch path. Host-level DNS gating cannot separate the two. A path-scoped grant limited to /*/*/releases/download/ would, which is the argument for building proxy path support rather than treating this host as permanently refused.
hosts.observed: FetchError: request to <url> failed, reason: getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN github.com — the denied arm of the Linux corpus run.

hosts.requester: @tensorflow/tfjs-node, chromedriver (also puppeteer and taiko on the earlier macOS pass)
hosts.detail: Refused because an attacker can rent a bucket under the same hostname and read back whatever a confined script writes there — the exfiltration criterion, not an integrity one. The two observed prefixes (/tensorflow/ and /chrome-for-testing-public/) are stable and single-tenant, so this is a second candidate for a path-scoped grant.
hosts.observed: Both artifacts requested in the denied arm of the Linux corpus run; libtensorflow logged as `* Downloading libtensorflow` immediately before the URL.

hosts.detail: A soft fetch that degrades rather than failing does not earn an entry: the CLI reports `failed to install amplify binary` with egress denied, but the install itself still exits 0.
hosts.observed: Error fetching release: getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN package.cli.amplify.aws, followed by `failed to install amplify binary`, in the denied arm of the Linux corpus run.

hosts.detail: Recorded as an evidenced candidate, not as a disqualification: no write-capable route or multi-tenant namespace has been established for it, and the fetch is a dedicated single-tenant vendor binary path. Whether it is admitted is a maintainer call, and it is deliberately left out of networkHosts until then. Note the requester is wrangler 1.x, which prints its own deprecation notice directing users to the `wrangler` package — so the demand may not survive the version it was measured on.
hosts.observed: Downloading release from <url>, then Error fetching release: getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN workers.cloudflare.com, in the denied arm of the Linux corpus run.
